summary: Evening elevated 5xx plateau caused by client retry storm and runtime watchdog deadlock
description: Issue summary: Starting ~18:10 UTC on 2026-03-12 we observed a sustained plateau of 5xx responses (~6-10% error rate) for requests routed to BrightBank's dedicated pool in us-east-1. API gateway showed elevated 502/504 counts and streaming sessions experienced partial resets. Impact: customer latency rose from 120ms median to 600ms and a significant fraction of requests returned 502/504; client application reported degraded UX and started its own retry loop, worsening load.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightBank tenant with reserved capacity in us-east-1
2) Run a synthetic workload mixing short streaming chats (keepalive pings every 12s) and synchronous generation requests at 80% of baseline throughput
3) Enable the customer's SDK hedged retry config (client retries at 100ms) to emulate aggressive client behavior
4) Observe API gateway error rate rise and backend runtime worker threads entering long NVML calls followed by watchdog timeouts
logs: apigw: 2026-03-12T18:14:22Z ERROR upstream returned 502 for tenant=brightbank-001 route=/v1/generate status_code=502 latency=432ms
runtime: 2026-03-12T18:15:01Z WARN worker[17] nvml_wait_for_compute: blocking for 1.2s
runtime: 2026-03-12T18:15:04Z ERROR watchdog: worker[17] missed-heartbeat -> soft-kill
client-metrics (from BrightBank): SDK hedged_retry_count spike from 20/min to 400/min at 18:12 UTC
investigation_notes: 18:20 UTC: PagerDuty alerted SRE to sustained 5xx plateau for BrightBank tenant. Initial triage pointed to accept-queue growth at apigw and repeated NVML block logs on a subset of runtime workers.

Hypothesis A: Client-side hedged retries produced a stampede that amplified transient backend latency into persistent overload. The customer SDK had recently enabled aggressive hedged retries (100ms) in a canary rollout.

Hypothesis B: A serving-runtime change in v2.3.1 introduced a blocking NVML path under specific mixed workload patterns; when worker threads block, watchdog escalates and restarts workers, causing transient capacity loss and backlog.

Correlations: Grafana shows a tight correlation between hedged_retry_count (client) and accept-queue-length; flamegraphs show worker threads spending ~40% time in nvml synchronous wait during the plateau window.

Repro: Engineering reproduced locally by running client retry scraper against a dedicated small pool and hit the same accept-queue growth and worker NVML waits. Instrumented runtime with async NVML shim removed the blocking behavior in test.
Linked evidence: Slack #support thread (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C07SUPPORT/p164709) and runtime PR that changed NVML call-path (PR 412) were both referenced.
Customer input: BrightBank confirmed they shipped an SDK change to hedged_retry=100ms on 2026-03-11 that progressively rolled to 30% of their fleet by 2026-03-12 evening.
Interim metrics: CPU on proxy nodes increased 2x, runtime worker restart rate increased from baseline 0.2/min to 3/min during the plateau.
Decision: Treat as Sev1 P1 due to dedicated-customer impact and need to coordinate immediate mitigations with customer and runtime engineers.
comments: Maya Patel (2026-03-12 18:25 UTC): Initial triage complete. Notified SRE and Eng on-call. Requested BrightBank to provide their SDK rollout logs and to temporarily reduce hedged retry config if possible.

SRE Oncall - Jordan Lee (2026-03-12 18:32 UTC): Increased apigw accept-queue cap and enabled emergency short-term shedding for tenant brightbank-001 to buy time. Observed partial improvement but error floor persisted.

Engineering - Daniel Kim (2026-03-12 19:05 UTC): Reproduced issue in staging with PR-412 enabled. Confirmed blocking NVML call under mixed streaming+sync workload. Preparing rollback for runtime v2.3.1 -> v2.3.0 for affected nodes.
BrightBank - Claire Thompson (2026-03-12 19:12 UTC): We are pausing the hedged retry rollout and reverting to previous SDK config for 100% of clients. Monitoring now.

Maya Patel (2026-03-12 19:40 UTC): After coordinated rollback of runtime on 4/6 dedicated hosts and customer rollback of hedged retries, 5xx rate dropped from ~8% to 0.7% over 12 minutes. Still monitoring.
Daniel Kim (2026-03-13 10:12 UTC): Filing follow-up INT ticket for a permanent runtime fix and adding e2e test to catch blocking NVML patterns.
resolution: Workaround applied: (1) BrightBank paused their SDK hedged-retry canary and reverted hedged_retry to 500ms; (2) SRE temporarily increased apigw accept-queue and enabled tenant-level shedding to protect other tenants; (3) Runtime team rolled back v2.3.1 on the affected dedicated pool to v2.3.0 and disabled the synchronous NVML path.
next_steps: 1) INT-341 (scheduled): Runtime team to implement async NVML shim and add defensive timeouts to NVML calls (owner: Daniel Kim), target: 2026-03-26
2) Update SDK guidance: Add recommended hedged_retry lower bound and backoff guidance to public docs and customer release notes (owner: DX), target: 2026-03-19
3) Add a Canary e2e that simulates mixed streaming + short-poll hedged retry workload to catch regressions in PR pipeline (owner: QA/Eng), target: 2026-03-20
4) Post-incident: Runbook update and postmortem doc on Confluence (owner: Support), target: 2026-03-18
